title: The Principles of Social Stratification
text: Social stratification describes a society’s categorization into rankings of socioeconomic tiers, which determine life chances and access to resources. These divisions—based on wealth, income, power, and prestige—are systematic and institutionalized, persisting across generations. Different models, such as caste systems or class structures, illustrate varying degrees of mobility; some are rigid and ascribed at birth, while others allow for greater movement based on achievement.
